annotations.title: TIA — I/O channel map of a PLC with tag matches

description: I/O channel map of ONE PLC, the base of a FAT/SAT I/O list: for every I/O device item reachable from the PLC (its own modules and onboard I/O, and the devices on its PROFINET IO systems) the address ranges with logical notation, the channels with logical addresses, the PLC tags that sit on them, and the I/O tags that sit on nothing. entries is one ordered list; kind is range (device, path, ioType, length, from, to, channels, status), channel (device, path, channel, address, bits, addressBasis, status, flags, tags) or tag (an I/O tag on no channel or range: table, name, address, status, reason). status: matched (one tag, exactly on the channel; on a range without channels, the tags inside it), unmatched (nothing on it), conflict (flags multipleTags, spansChannels, partial), unresolved (no address: unresolved says why), channels (a range whose channels are listed as their own entries) and unparsed (an I/O address that is not valid). Each tag carries match: exact, spans, partial or inRange. Channel addresses are DERIVED from the address range of the item and the channel number, never read from TIA (addressBasis derived): verify them against the hardware configuration. A range's length is in BYTES (Openness reports bits; the map converts, rounding up); tia_device_tree's raw addresses[].length stays in BITS. summary and coverage describe the WHOLE result: check coverage on every page. coverage.complete false, any unresolved or unparsed entry, any coverage.unreadable entry, an omission marker or an unfinished page walk means the map, and any FAT/SAT list built from it, is NOT complete: report the gap, never guess an address. coverage.limits is always present and does not change complete: PROFIBUS DP master systems and devices outside the PLC's PROFINET IO systems are not read, so an unmatched tag may belong there. Paging: limit (1..1000) and cursor page the entries; a page adds total and nextCursor: pass it back as cursor until nextCursor is null; cursor_stale: restart without cursor; invalid_cursor: pass it unchanged. Each page re-walks the whole PLC, so paging bounds the size of the response, not the time of the walk. Start with limit 100 to 200: a larger page can exceed the response budget, then arrives with an omission marker and NO nextCursor: retry with a smaller limit. Requires a connected project. Maps to GET /plcs/{plc}/io-map?limit=&cursor=. Read-only (class R). Long operation: may answer status:"running" + jobId — then call tia_job_status.

cursor.description: the nextCursor of the previous page, passed back exactly as received; it is opaque, so never invent, build or edit one (omit it for the first page, and omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)

limit.description: page size, an integer from 1 to 1000; pass it to read the list in pages (omit both limit and cursor for the whole list)
